approachQuestion.prompt:
Closest appointment slot

Given a strictly increasing read-only integer array a of available time slots and integer requested, return the slot value minimizing absolute distance. Break ties toward the smaller value. 1 <= n <= 200000; slots and requested lie in [-10^9,10^9]. Examples: [2,8,15], requested=11 -> 8; requested=12 -> 15; [2,8], requested=5 -> 2. Prefer worst-case probes, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Find lower_bound(requested) iteratively. Compare that successor, if present, with its predecessor, if present, and return the closer value, preferring the predecessor on ties.
options.feedback: Sorted order confines the nearest value to the insertion-point neighbors; tie policy belongs in the final comparison.

options.text: Recursively find the insertion point using index bounds, then compare the same neighbors.
options.feedback: The answer is correct, but recursion consumes avoidable stack space.

options.text: Always return the lower_bound successor, returning the last slot only if no successor exists.
options.feedback: For [2,8,15], requested=11, successor 15 is farther than predecessor 8.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Analyze the iterative lower-bound search plus at most two distance calculations. Use signed 64-bit differences. Random access and arithmetic are constant time; no copies or stack. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

feedback.reason: One lower-bound search is followed by at most two distance checks.
details: Finding the insertion boundary needs O(log(n+1)) comparisons. At most two 64-bit distance calculations follow, adding constant work. Only bounds, two candidate values, and the current best are retained.
“O(log(n + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Sorted order confines the nearest value to the insertion-point neighbors; tie policy belongs in the final comparison.
“O(n*n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: One lower-bound search plus two neighbor checks has logarithmic work and scalar state, not quadratic pair work or linear storage.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The closest neighbor cannot generally be located without the logarithmic insertion-point search.
